questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Something different from Denmark, new culture, warmer than Denmark didn't hurt either, learning a new language (which I didn't have time for at all though).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I met really lovely people and Andalusia is such a beautiful region, but the school itself / the academic part was a 1/10.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy since everything is chaotic, unorganized, and in Spanish.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Again not a lot of orientation, and the little orientation that there was still wasn't a lot. You have to figure it out on your own or ask other exchange students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are a lot websites and apps you can use to find a place to live, it's fairly easy to find something if you aren't picky. There's also a group chat on whatsapp you'll get added to, where students leaving post their homes to students that are incoming.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That there are a LOT of scammers, so make sure that the one you're looking at is legit. Also most of the apartments are horribly build and heating isn't assured, so bring very warm clothes for the cold nights :)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very hard finding the courses, you had to go to a website that isn't linked on the official one to access the curriculum that I needed for my home university. So that could be made a bit better :)

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to make a learning agreement.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write the International Relations Office on WhatsApp and get answers fairly quickly, or you could go to a google meets meeting, they're open a couple of hours every day.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you aren't good at spanish don't choose the spanish courses. The dialect in this part of Spain is hard to understand haha. Also keep writing if you aren't getting replies.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had one amazing teacher (Alejandro Romero), who was just amazing. The rest, not so much. Also the exam-form is just not very good / it's not meant to show how much you know or have learned, its how well you can memorize.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Do not go here as a masters student and expect to learn or be challenged. Not as a bachelor student either actually. Some of the courses sure, they're fine, but the general consensus of all the exchange students I've spoken to is that it isn't great.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some were very much the same, but in general the organisation was just not the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Theory of Democracy: Gender and Interculturality, Sociology of Populations and Migrations, Political Systems in the Maghreb, International Organisations, and Contemporary Sociological Theory.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Contemporary Sociological Theory has the greatest teacher Alejandro, so I would definitely recommend that course - the exam is a bit hard though. But he is amazing. 
I strongly advice against international organisations, because of one of the teachers made it very uncomfortable. Also don't expect to learn anything from theory of democracy - but there's good literature.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't really have any unexpected. Maybe creation of cards/access to the different organisations. That costs around 10 euro pr. organisation.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I mean we didn't really get many offers from the uni. But there's three main organisations that make trips etc. for erasmus students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Trips to morocco, ferias, other big cities in Spain, parties, all sorts of stuff.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depends on who you are I guess haha, if you're fine with kind of unorganized events, then go on the trips etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Obviously the entirety of Granada - Alhambra, Albaicin, sunset at San Miguel Alto etc. etc. Also just the cities in the mountains like Ronda, or by the coast like Cadiz or Estepona. Also Malaga. Go to Madrid or Barcelona for some days. Just enjoy espanaaaa.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fine, but I'm also a night owl in general. So it was fine.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk with those in your classes! And go out. People are way more open to talking to strangers than in Denmark fx.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Siesta / the entire city shutting down for hours was a bit weird to get used to. Also the dinner time (21-22) took some time getting used to. Also they don't speak english. Also nothing is organized, you literally cannot count on a lot of things, even if it is "officials".

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The very chill laid back vibe. Manana manana. Calma calma.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't go if you have to take 30 ECTS, tinto de verano is what you drink in granada (not sangria), and enjoy one of the most beautiful cities

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can get cheaper language education through the student organisations.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people, the friends I got <3

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning Spanish and getting used to an unorganised life haha.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
